payload.description:
## Context

Asked on 2026-08-22 to dispatch at a `maximum` tier so two models would appear on one board, I reported that a run could not choose a tier and that per-lane models were not dispatchable. **Both claims were wrong**, and the reason I got them wrong is a documentation gap rather than a reading failure.

The owner corrected it: *"how did model tier not exist, there is a full kit that instantiates an agent using a model that fits the tier."*

## What exists, proved

A `[[runner.agents]]` entry takes `tier` and `vendor`. Two agents declared in a scratch config, with no code change:

```text
claude-max   tier=maximum  source=agent tier -> claude-fable-5
claude-mid   tier=medium   source=agent tier -> claude-sonnet-5
```

And `[runner] decider` selects a different agent for decider invocations, so two models run **concurrently**:

```text
lanes    -> agent=claude-max   tier=maximum  model=claude-fable-5
decider  -> agent=claude-mid   tier=medium   model=claude-sonnet-5
```

`_parse_model_tier` reads the key, `tier_source` records `agent tier`, and `models.model_for` resolves it through `.basicly/core/models/model-map.json`.

## The gap

`basicly.toml`'s `[runner]` block documents `default`, `max_agent_processes` and a full commented `[[runner.agents]]` example that covers `name`, `command`, `prompt_via`, `model`, `tier`, `vendor`, `sandbox`, `approval`, `git_name` and `git_email`.

It does not mention `decider` at all. Verified two ways: `grep decider basicly.toml` returns four hits and every one is prose about the decider agent's *corpus*, not the runner key; and `config.py:1627` reads `section.get("decider")` off the `[runner]` section, so the key is live.

So the one key that answers "can two models run at once" is the one key the file does not name, sitting beside keys it does.

## Why a comment and not a note-to-self

This file is the surface a consumer of `basicly install` reads to learn what it may configure. A live key it does not document is not discoverable by reading it, which is the only way a consumer learns anything here. `[runner] default_tier` is documented and got used; `[runner] decider` is not and did not.

## What remains genuinely absent

Two lanes **in the same lane set** cannot run different models: `supervise.py:2010` resolves one spec and dispatches every admitted lane with it. That is `basicly-a3yi`'s territory and is unaffected by this record. The per-role split - lanes against decider - is what already works.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `grep -n 'decider' basicly.toml`
2. Read every hit.

**Observed.** Four hits, all prose about the decider's intake corpus. No `[runner] decider` key and no commented example of one.

**Control.** `grep -n 'max_agent_processes' basicly.toml` returns a commented example, so the file does document optional `[runner]` keys and the absence is specific rather than a house style.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a reader looks for how to give a role its own agent, `basicly.toml` SHALL name `[runner] decider` with an example.
- WHEN a key is read from a config section, IT SHALL appear in that file, and a check SHALL compare the loader's accepted keys against the file rather than leaving it to a reader.
- WHERE two models can run at once, THE FILE SHALL say so where an author is choosing agents, because that is the question the keys answer together and neither answers alone.

## Scope

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Trigger

When an author reads `basicly.toml` to learn how to give a role its own model, I want the file to name the `[runner] decider` key with an example, so I can configure two models to run at once without guessing.

## Context

Asked on 2026-08-22 to dispatch at a `maximum` tier so two models would appear on one board, I reported that a run could not choose a tier and that per-lane models were not dispatchable. **Both claims were wrong**, and the reason I got them wrong is a documentation gap rather than a reading failure.

The owner corrected it: *"how did model tier not exist, there is a full kit that instantiates an agent using a model that fits the tier."*

## What exists, proved

A `[[runner.agents]]` entry takes `tier` and `vendor`. Two agents declared in a scratch config, with no code change:

```text
claude-max   tier=maximum  source=agent tier -> claude-fable-5
claude-mid   tier=medium   source=agent tier -> claude-sonnet-5
```

And `[runner] decider` selects a different agent for decider invocations, so two models run **concurrently**:

```text
lanes    -> agent=claude-max   tier=maximum  model=claude-fable-5
decider  -> agent=claude-mid   tier=medium   model=claude-sonnet-5
```

`_parse_model_tier` reads the key, `tier_source` records `agent tier`, and `models.model_for` resolves it through `.basicly/core/models/model-map.json`.

## The gap

`basicly.toml`'s `[runner]` block documents `default`, `max_agent_processes` and a full commented `[[runner.agents]]` example that covers `name`, `command`, `prompt_via`, `model`, `tier`, `vendor`, `sandbox`, `approval`, `git_name` and `git_email`.

It does not mention `decider` at all. Verified two ways: `grep decider basicly.toml` returns four hits and every one is prose about the decider agent's *corpus*, not the runner key; and `config.py:1627` reads `section.get("decider")` off the `[runner]` section, so the key is live.

So the one key that answers "can two models run at once" is the one key the file does not name, sitting beside keys it does.

## Why a comment and not a note-to-self

This file is the surface a consumer of `basicly install` reads to learn what it may configure. A live key it does not document is not discoverable by reading it, which is the only way a consumer learns anything here. `[runner] default_tier` is documented and got used; `[runner] decider` is not and did not.

## What remains genuinely absent

Two lanes **in the same lane set** cannot run different models: `supervise.py:2010` resolves one spec and dispatches every admitted lane with it. That is `basicly-a3yi`'s territory and is unaffected by this record. The per-role split - lanes against decider - is what already works.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `grep -n 'decider' basicly.toml`
2. Read every hit.

**Observed.** Four hits, all prose about the decider's intake corpus. No `[runner] decider` key and no commented example of one.

**Control.** `grep -n 'max_agent_processes' basicly.toml` returns a commented example, so the file does document optional `[runner]` keys and the absence is specific rather than a house style.

## Scope

- `basicly.toml`
- `.scripts/check_docs_claims.py`
- `tests/test_config.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- budget: `70000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Grep the config for every key the runner loader reads and find each one documented, with a control key removed from the file to show the check fails rather than passing vacuously.

The file states, where an author is choosing agents, that two models can run at once through this split.

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a metered dispatch whose adapter declares a streaming usage format when it runs then each event is observed while the process is still running and both the stall watchdog clock and the session spend meter are driven from those events rather than from git state alone and the terminal usage totals extract_usage reports are unchanged and given a stream line that is not valid in the platform encoding then the reader replaces the undecodable bytes and keeps reading rather than dying silently with tests
payload.description:
## Context

Every metered lane already asks its agent CLI for a per-turn event stream, and the harness already
throws that stream away. Established 2026-08-06 at d809229.

- `CLAUDE_STREAM_JSON` (runner.py:83-86) is `--output-format stream-json --verbose`, documented in
  place as *"JSONL events, one per turn, ending in the same result object. The only claude envelope
  that carries per-turn usage."*
- `CODEX_JSONL` (runner.py:87) is `--json`: *"JSONL event stream with turn.completed usage."*
- `supervise._dispatch_lane` (supervise.py:2370) passes `capture_usage=True`, so both flags are on
  for every real lane.

`runner.run` then collects the whole thing with `proc.communicate(input=stdin, timeout=timeout)`
(runner.py:1042), which by definition blocks until the process exits and returns one buffer.
`extract_usage` parses only the **terminal** result object for totals. Every intermediate event -
per-turn usage, tool calls, progress - is received and dropped.

**The workaround is already documented as a workaround.** `lane_activity` (supervise.py:2136-2143):
*"Reading the agent's stdout would be the other signal, but the runner drains its pipes only after
the process is down (basicly-kjc5.15), so there is nothing incremental to sample; commits and file
writes are both cheaper."* So the git-state probe, and its blind spot where a lane running a long
test suite reads as idle, exist **because** the better signal is not consumed.

## Why this is the prerequisite, not a nice-to-have

`basicly-yvx9` records that terminal authority sits on the one signal that cannot tell a working
lane from a wedged one, and that its own step 2 - making the idle bound terminal - is blocked on
measuring `lane_activity`'s quiet tail. Consuming the stream removes that blocker outright: an
event is proof of life whether or not any file changed.

It also changes **what the right bound is**. Per-turn usage means the D3 spend ceiling can bind
*during* a dispatch instead of only at pass boundaries. Today it cannot, and the cost is on the
record: a 20,000,000-token grant on `basicly-vhft` was overshot to 22,164,783 because
`spend_status` is consulted before a pass and recorded after it, with nothing in between. Tokens
accrue monotonically and are the resource that actually matters, so a spend bound is strictly
better than a clock.

## The wall clock does not become irrelevant

A runaway agent looping edit -> test -> edit -> test on one file is **maximally active** by any
liveness measure. Streaming makes it visible; it does not bound it. What changes is the wall
clock's *job*: from the working bound it is today - calibrated at 95% of the real work
distribution, see `basicly-yvx9` - to a last-resort backstop for the pathological case, a process
that hangs holding the pipe or a stream that stops while the process does not exit. It stays, at a
value where it never fires in normal operation.

## Implementation hazard, and it is the one to design against first

`communicate()` exists to avoid pipe deadlock. Reading incrementally needs a reader per pipe, and
`runner.run` passes `text=True` to `Popen`, so **decoding happens on those reader threads**. That is
exactly `basicly-6gkg`: a `UnicodeDecodeError` on a reader thread kills the thread and the caller
sees a successful run with no output. Set `errors="replace"` explicitly on the stream reader, and
test it with a byte sequence that is invalid in the platform encoding - otherwise this reintroduces
6gkg in the single place it would be hardest to notice, because the symptom is silence.

Second constraint: the events carry the agent's own text, so `redact_secrets` has to run on the
incremental path too, not only on the final buffer (basicly-3p2i).

## What to build

1. Read stdout line by line while the dispatch runs, parse each line as an event, keep stderr
   drained on its own reader so neither pipe can fill.
2. Feed the events to a sink the caller supplies. Two consumers exist already and want it:
   `StallWatchdog` (an event restarts its clock, replacing the git fingerprint) and the spend
   meter (per-turn usage accrues against the grant mid-dispatch).
3. Keep the terminal result object doing exactly what it does now, so `extract_usage` and every
   existing total stay byte-identical - this must be additive, and the existing spend numbers must
   not move.
4. Surface it: a lane's live progress is what `basicly-8vy4` and the supervised-run observability
   complaints both reduce to.

An adapter with no stream format - `COPILOT_SESSION_STORE` measures out of band - keeps today's
behaviour, so the sink must be optional per spec rather than assumed.

## Steps to Reproduce

```sh
uv run python -c "
from basicly import runner
spec = next(s for s in runner.BUILTIN_SPECS if s.name == 'claude')
print(spec.usage_format)
print(runner._USAGE_FLAGS[spec.usage_format])"
```

The flags requesting a per-turn stream are present; `runner.run` reads the result with
`proc.communicate`, so nothing observes a single intermediate event.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/runner.py`
- `src/basicly/supervise.py`
- `tests/test_runner.py`
- `tests/test_supervise.py`

payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Measured 2026-08-05 at `d31f6bd`, from the repo's own committed call ledger:

```
uv run python -c "
import json, pathlib, statistics
rows = [json.loads(l) for l in pathlib.Path('.basicly/ledger/tracker-usage.jsonl').read_text().splitlines() if l.strip()]
ms = sorted(r['duration_ms'] for r in rows if r.get('duration_ms') is not None)
print(len(ms), 'calls; median', statistics.median(ms), 'p95', ms[int(len(ms)*0.95)])"
```

Observed — 1,420 recorded engine calls to `br`: **median 14.2 ms**, p95 **110.3 ms**, total 50.4 s.
`tracker_usage.py:337-373` confirms the timer wraps the whole subprocess spawn, so this is the
honest end-to-end cost.

Expected — §10's figures describe the distribution they were drawn from.

## The defect

`docs/design/work-tracker.md` §10 cites **113 ms** per `br` call and concludes an owned tracker
would be **"~175× cheaper"**. 113 ms is not the typical call; it is approximately the **p95**. The
median is 14.2 ms.

Against a full 2.1 MB fold of the current ledger, measured the same day at **5.8–7.6 ms** for an
open-read-parse, the real advantage is **~2.4×**, not 175×. And a fold is O(events) while a `br`
spawn is roughly constant, so the ratio *narrows* as the ledger grows unless an index amortises it —
which §10's own framing acknowledges but the headline number does not.

## Why this matters beyond tidiness

**Speed is one of the stated arguments for `v0.8.0`.** A 175× claim justifies a release; a 2.4×
claim does not, and nothing else in the section flags that. The arguments that *do* hold are
untouched and sufficient on their own: ownership of the harness's own state (§1), the licence rider
restricting a class of users, and twelve paid-for defects now carried as R1–R8 requirements. The
correction therefore removes a bad reason for a good decision, rather than the decision.

## The class, not just the instance

This is the same shape as the context-window constant (`basicly-23ep`): a number that was plausible
when written, was never re-measured, and had already been refuted by the repo's own ledger. There
the constant said 200000 while run records held 223221; here the design says 113 ms while the call
ledger holds a 14.2 ms median. Both were mechanically detectable the whole time. §10's own title is
"Speed and scaling — **measured, not assumed**", which is the part that did not survive contact with
the ledger it was measured from.

Two figures in §9.1/§10 are stale by the same mechanism and should be refreshed in the same pass:
they describe the tracker as **330 records / 749–761 KB**, against a measured **603 records /
2,112,691 bytes** — 1.8× stale in count and 2.8× in bytes. The maximum line length is unchanged.

## Fix shape

- Restate §10 with the distribution rather than a single sample: median, p95, and n, naming which
  statistic each comparison uses.
- Refresh the record/byte counts in §9.1 and §10, and say when they were taken.
- State the direction of travel: a spawn is ~constant, a fold is O(events), so the gap closes as the
  ledger grows and the index is what recovers it.
- Do **not** simply paste in fresher numbers — that is `23ep`'s anti-pattern one generation on. A
  figure in this document that can be derived from a ledger we own should be generated and gated,
  the way `.scripts/docs_claims.py` already generates the plan's structural table and
  `architecture.md`'s always-on sizes. That is the only version of this fix that cannot rot again.

## Scope

- `docs/design/work-tracker.md`
- `.scripts/docs_claims.py`
- `tests/test_docs_claims.py`

payload.description:
## Context

Reproduced 2026-08-21 on three consecutive ship advances. Two of the three refused:

```text
the release record was refused: basicly-rn0o.7's release-record artifact does not
validate: $.unsupported[0]: Additional properties are not allowed
('suggested_wording' was unexpected)
```

`basicly-rn0o.14` failed identically. `basicly-rn0o.13` passed, reporting `5 claim(s) bound, 3 unsupported`, so the failure is non-deterministic rather than total - which is what makes the cause the missing declaration rather than a wrong schema.

## The cause, and it is a contract asymmetry

`release-record.schema.json` sets `additionalProperties: false` on `unsupported[]` items and requires exactly `claim` and `why`. The curator source's `output_contract` says only *"each unsupported claim named"*. It never names the two fields, so the model chooses a shape, and a helpful extra key is the natural choice.

A producer told to emit an artifact and not told its field set will invent one. The consumer then refuses, and SHIP has already merged, so the refusal costs the release record rather than blocking anything - which is why this has been silent.

## Why the schema is not the thing to widen

`suggested_wording` is a claim about what the notes *should* say. The curator's stated job is to bind a claim to evidence or drop it, never to soften or rewrite one. Admitting the field would admit the behaviour the role exists to refuse.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the curator is briefed, ITS OUTPUT CONTRACT SHALL name every field the release-record schema requires and state that the object admits no other key.
- WHEN a curator reply carries a key the schema forbids, THE ENGINE SHALL name the key and the artifact kind, as it already does.
- WHEN three consecutive ship advances run, EVERY release record SHALL validate.
- WHERE another agent source produces a schema-validated artifact, ITS CONTRACT SHALL name that schema's field set too, so this is fixed as a class rather than one instance.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/agents/curator/agent.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/agents/blocks/*.block.yaml`
- `tests/test_agent_lint.py`

payload.description:
## Context

The wall layout landed and its loop region is the one question it still cannot answer. Measured on this repository 2026-08-21:

```text
THE LOOP   intake 8 · classify 0 · decompose 0 · build 0 · verify 0 · validate 0 · ship 0
           phase covers 8 of 234 units
```

`board_facts.PHASE_LIMIT` is 8, and the number is a cost rather than a taste. `loop_state.read_node_state` is the only route to `derive_phase`, and it reads the whole event log **seven times per record** - 591 ms over 20 records, measured - so 234 units is about 138 s against a 4.7 s build. The cap is at the ready front because that is the column a wall board is read for, and outside it `phase` stays absent rather than guessed, which is right.

The consequence is that a board whose whole point is *where is the work* reports every phase but intake as zero, and a reader cannot tell that from a genuinely idle factory.

## The shape of the fix

One fold, then a derivation per record over the folded state. `derive_phase` is a pure function of five values already in the fold; what costs is re-reading the log for each of them. The seam does not exist: `read_node_state` is per record by construction.

This is the same measurement discipline the fold already has - `board_snapshot` folds once and a spy pins the count - so the acceptance is a spy, not a stopwatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a phase map is built for every active record, THE READER SHALL fold the event log once, and a spy SHALL pin the fold count at one.
- WHEN the map is built, EVERY PHASE SHALL come from `loop_state.derive_phase` rather than from a second derivation.
- WHEN the map covers the whole active population, THE BUILD SHALL stay under the declared cap, and the demonstration SHALL print the measured duration.
- WHERE a record cannot be derived, ITS PHASE SHALL be absent rather than guessed, and the caption SHALL name how many units carry one.
- WHEN the cap is no longer needed, `PHASE_LIMIT` SHALL be removed rather than raised, so no reader is left believing a bound still applies.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/loop_state.py`
- `src/basicly/board_facts.py`
- `tests/test_loop_state.py`
- `tests/test_board_facts.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `140000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: `uv run basicly board --out <redacted:posix-absolute-path>` printing a build time under the cap, and the emitted snapshot carrying a phase on every active unit rather than on eight.

The file says so itself: "silently scoring the old anchors against new text is how a recall number becomes fiction". The instrument is unusable until this is paid off, and nothing in `verify` notices, because the inventory check is not a gate.

## Acceptance
- `recall_eval.py --inventory` exits 0 on a clean tree.
- The inventory check runs in `basicly verify` so it cannot drift again unnoticed.

- `.scripts/recall_rules.toml`

- `basicly.d/`

payload.description: Proven by CI run 32632831403: PermissionError WinError 32 at base_lock.py:157 path.unlink in hold's finally, raised in a dispatch thread while a waiter's holder() read_text held the file open. Windows refuses to delete an open file, so the holder dies unreleased, waiters poll for WAIT_S (1200 s) and then refuse - a real concurrent-dispatch outage, not only a flaky test. Second race in the same family: os.open O_CREAT|O_EXCL on a delete-pending file raises PermissionError, crashing a waiter's _take. Fix: bounded retry on the release, and treat PermissionError at the exclusive create as busy. Assert both by injection per the platform-hermetic rule.

payload.description:
## Context

Step 5 of the cutover, and the one that actually removes `br` from the engine. Measured
2026-08-07 against `main` @ `b97a653`.

`comments` is the single largest remaining dependency: 26 of the engine 55 `_run_br` call
sites, and 714 of 1568 recorded br invocations (45% of all traffic) per
`docs/design/work-tracker.md` §3.0. Split by direction it is 22 `comments add` and 6
`comments list`.

## The surface is 89% harness transport

Measured over the live tracker (1834 comments across 427 of 644 beads):

| | count | share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[harness-*]` markers | **1646** | **89%** |
| human prose | 188 | 10% |

By kind: policy 828, wait 259, run 225, cost 154, decision 113, info 36, sizing 19,
overrun 12. Every one is harness-owned state - checkpoint approvals, grants, gate
records, rework counters, needs-input, the human-wait clock, dispatch records, spend
rollups - using a beads comment purely as transport.

This is what plan §10 standing constraint anticipated: "Land evidence as `[harness-*]`
comment markers - a format we own, which migrates with us - not as tracker fields." The
markers were chosen so this migration would be possible. It is now due.

## The destination already exists and already holds the data

`events.py` declares `KIND_COMMENT` and a dedicated `KIND_DISPATCH`, and the step-1
import (commit `b97a653`) already wrote **1831 comment events** into the ledger. So this
is not a data migration - the facts are in both stores. It is a seam change: the engine
must write and read its own markers natively rather than spawning br.

`br.py` records why that is tractable: the write surface is one funnel
(`run_br`/`try_run_br`) and the record-read surface is one function (`read_record`), so
this is an edit to a seam rather than to 26 callers.

## Deliberately out of scope

The 188 human comments. A human writing prose on a bead runs `br` directly; the engine
never spawns that. Removing the engine dependency does not require removing the human one,
and conflating them is how this grows into a general-purpose tracker - an explicit
non-goal (plan §2).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the engine at tracker mode owned when a checkpoint approval or gate record or grant or rework counter or dispatch record is written then it is written as a ledger event and read back from the ledger with no br comments spawn, and a test proves the engine completes that write and read with br absent from PATH

## Scope

- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `src/basicly/br.py`
- `src/basicly/run_record.py`
- `src/basicly/decisions.py`
- `tests/test_policy.py`
- `tests/test_br_seam.py`
payload.title: Carry the harness markers as ledger events instead of beads comments

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a task needs a seat, I want the engine to pick one by comparing declared facts, so I can route work without asking a model to report its own fitness.

## Requirements

R1. No model ever reports its own suitability for a task, because a persuadable scheduler is not a scheduler.
R2. A match that could not apply an axis says which axis it could not apply, because a silently partial match is worse than none.
R3. Adding a fifth axis later does not change the three axes that already exist.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When an agent source declares its tools, then the catalog lint accepts the declaration and a missing one is reported. [check: `tests/test_catalog_lint.py`]
- When the engine matches a task, then it compares the scope globs, the integrity level, the model tier and the tools, and returns one seat or none. [check: `tests/test_seat_match.py`]
- When an axis cannot be evaluated because nothing declares it, then the match result names that axis as unbound. [check: `tests/test_seat_match.py`]
- When no seat matches, then the task stays ready and the reason names the axis that excluded every seat. [check: `tests/test_seat_match.py`]

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_seat_match.py -q`

## Design notes

Architecture section 31A.6 and D-47. Three axes exist: the scope globs on the planned child, the integrity level `integrity._RULES` assigns, and the tier on the agent source. Only the tools axis is new. The tier axis is inert at spawn until basicly-a3yi lands, so a match on it reports unbound rather than pretending.

## Context

Four operating traps lived only in one agent's local memory on one machine, so a second machine or a second agent re-discovers each at the price of a round. Probed 2026-08-29 with `rg -c` over `.basicly/core/`, AGENTS.md and the ledger (control: `positive control` = 8 hits): `setsid` 0, `scratch clone` 0, `2x` wall-clock rule 0, `headroom` 0. Each has a code form that is a separate record; this record is the interim skill bullet so the knowledge is in the repo today.

1. A supervisor started through an agent tool's background job dies at that tool's ceiling (10 minutes for one host) mid-round; three lanes died with it on 2026-08-28. Detach it (`setsid nohup ... & disown`) and watch the log. Code form: `loop supervise --detach`.
2. `basicly release --dry-run` runs no commit gate (basicly-vwh3aq, open); the proof is a scratch clone that applies the release steps, stages, and runs the pre-commit framework and the whole suite.
3. A wall-clock cap in a test must clear the slowest CI runner by 2x or it is a flake generator (basicly-7aler3: 3.0 s cap measured 0.48 s locally, 3.1 s on windows-latest).
4. Measure the module-size and comment-density headroom of every file a change will touch before writing (`.scripts/headroom.py <files>`); the two ratchets pull opposite ways and paying them after the code is written is the slowest order.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the `harness-loop` skill's supervise section is read, IT SHALL say how to start a supervisor so no agent tool ceiling can kill it, and what to watch in its log.
- WHEN the `release-process` skill is read, IT SHALL carry the scratch-clone proof as the step before handing the owner the release command, and name basicly-vwh3aq as the record that retires the step.
- WHEN the `test-discipline` skill's Determinism section is read, IT SHALL carry the 2x rule for a wall-clock cap.
- WHEN the `python` skill is read, IT SHALL say to measure headroom with `.scripts/headroom.py` before placing code.
- WHEN `uv run basicly skills-check --all-default-roots` and `uv run basicly catalog lint` run, THEY SHALL pass.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/skills/harness-loop/skill.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/skills/release-process/skill.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/skills/test-discipline/skill.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/skills/python/skill.yaml`
- `.claude/skills/**`
- `.agents/skills/**`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.changed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L1`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: `rg -n 'setsid|scratch clone|2x|headroom.py' .basicly/core/skills/` prints one hit per skill named above.

payload.description:
## Context

Session retro, 2026-08-06. Two mistakes in one session, each with a concrete guidance gap.

**A grant sized on an assumption overshot its ceiling.** 20M was granted for the `v0.7.1` phase
on the reasoning that the driving session would write the code; `loop run` dispatched a metered
runner instead and spent 22,164,783. The autonomy *level* covers checkpoints - it does not decide
who writes the code. The skill discussed grants without ever saying how to size the budget.

**A leaf-shaped bead filed as a `feature` stalled before any code was written.**
`--work-type feature` parked `basicly-rupz` at decompose demanding a child plan and provisioned
no worktree. The phase table listed the five work types without saying that the choice decides
whether the loop asks for children.

The second is the sharper lesson: that rule already existed in an agent's own memory and still
did not bind. Guidance an operator has to remember is guidance the repo is missing - which is the
same argument `basicly-ze8z` makes for externalizing operator knowledge.

## What changed

`.basicly/core/skills/harness-loop/skill.yaml`, projected to both skill roots:

- A **Size a grant's token budget from the ledger** section with the query that reads the mean per
  executed lane out of `run-records.json`, the rule to budget `mean x lanes` plus headroom for one
  wall-clock death (16-21M measured), and both recorded failure modes - the "I will do the coding
  myself" assumption, and the fact that `spend_status` is read before a pass and recorded after it
  so the ceiling cannot stop a dispatch already running.
- The **intake** row now says to classify by shape: one coherent change is a `task`, only work
  that fans out into separately landable children is a `feature`, and a `feature` blocks at
  decompose and provisions nothing. Includes the recovery (`br update <id> -t task`).

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/skills/harness-loop/skill.yaml`
- `.claude/skills/harness-loop/SKILL.md`
- `.agents/skills/harness-loop/SKILL.md`

## Context
When a lane is landed and clean, I want basicly worktree cleanup to remove it without --force, so a clean lane never needs a discard flag that the auto-mode classifier refuses.

## Finding
Reported by the handily session via the Orchestrator, 2026-11-16, on a landed clean lane: git status --short shows only '?? .basicly/ledger/redirect'. 'basicly worktree cleanup statemark' exits 1 with "worktree 'statemark' has uncommitted changes; commit them or pass force to discard:" followed by 15 lines of git-ignored generated folders such as '!! mods/handily-board/.claude-plugin/types/handily-workitems/'. The tool counts ignored entries (!!) and its own redirect file as uncommitted work, so every clean lane needs --force.

## Fix
Ignore !! entries and the tool's own .basicly/ledger/redirect when cleanup checks for uncommitted work. Not claimed and not built.
payload.title: Let worktree cleanup ignore git-ignored files and its own redirect file

payload.description:
## Context

Read-only survey on 2026-08-26 of the nine loop skills (`.basicly/core/skills/*/skill.yaml`) and the four always-on fragments that mention the loop, the tracker, worktrees or gates, 61 claims checked against the code. Eleven are refuted; ten CONFIRMED by reading the code or `--help`, one SUSPECTED. Two would make an agent act wrongly (2, 4). Edit the YAML sources only, then `basicly skills-build --all-default-roots`, `basicly build`, and the projection gates.

1. `harness-client/skill.yaml:54-56` says `board serve` binds the loopback only and answers GET alone, a POST is 405. `src/basicly/board_cli.py:136` (`actions=not args.no_actions`, default on), `board_serve.py:402,411`, `board_actions.py:349` (405 only with `--no-actions`), `--bind` on `board serve --help`. Replacement: "It takes no lock and writes no file, but by default it registers one POST route that runs the basicly command an operator submits - pass `--no-actions` for an unattended wall, and leave `--bind` unset so it stays on the loopback."
2. `fragments/project/harness-loop.fragment.yaml` body: phases "(intake → classify → decompose → build → verify → ship → teardown → retro)". `src/basicly/loop_state.py:31` PHASES = intake, classify, decompose, build, verify, validate, ship, done; the `harness-loop` skill description itself says teardown and retro are not phases. Replacement: "(intake → classify → decompose → build → verify → validate → ship → done)".
3. `harness-loop/skill.yaml:5` and the phase table `:186-194` omit `validate`. `loop.py:451` `_on_validate`, `:470` blocks with `needs_input="validation"`; `validate-as-consumer/skill.yaml:12` covers phase `validate`. Add a table row between verify and ship: "| **validate** | the merged unit owes the consumer check its integrity level requires; the engine dispatches a validator and blocks on `needs input: validation` until a verdict is recorded | `basicly policy gate <id>` to inspect; a failed validate repairs in the lane's worktree and re-lands (see `validate-as-consumer`, `repair-in-place`) |" and fix the description's arrow chain.
4. `catalog-authoring/skill.yaml:41` "Project + verify: `basicly skills-build` then `basicly skills-check`." `src/basicly/skills.py:181-183` writes `.claude/skills` only without a flag; `basicly.toml:415-416` `projection-skills` checks both roots. Replacement: "Project + verify: `basicly skills-build --all-default-roots` then `basicly skills-check --all-default-roots` - bare, both touch only `.claude/skills`, and the `projection-skills` gate checks both roots."
5. `harness-loop/skill.yaml:54-55` "one `chore(ledger)` commit". `merge.py:654` commits `chore(beads): ...`. Replacement: "one `chore(beads)` commit".
6. `decompose-plan/skill.yaml:24` "Acceptance criteria | absent, **or not in EARS**". `plan_gate.py:194` checks presence only; `grep -ri ears src/` is empty (positive control: `demonstration` has many hits). Replacement row: "| Acceptance criteria | absent | The gate checks presence only, so the EARS discipline is yours to keep |".
7. `harness-loop/skill.yaml:401-404` "Two `VERDICT` lines mean fix this first". `cli.py:2966-3269` joins at least eight blockers with `; ` on one line. Replacement: "A `VERDICT: not ready - ...` line joins every blocker it found with `; ` - a dirty base, an unrecognised config key, a metered runner with no token budget, a spent or unmeterable grant, an unapproved root checkpoint, or no open child in the band. Read the whole line."
8. `release-process/skill.yaml:19-21` enumerates four pin files. `release.py:81-86` has `PIN_FILES` plus `PIN_GLOBS = ("docs/how-to/*.md",)`, with the comment that the enumeration is what failed. Add "and every page under `docs/how-to/`".
9. `harness-loop/skill.yaml:194` ship row omits the demonstration guard. `loop.py:646-648` blocks ship with `needs_input="demonstration"` before the not-landed guard. Add: "Two guards run first and both block with no side effects: the recorded demonstration must still select something (`needs input: demonstration`), and the branch must already be merged."
10. `harness-loop/skill.yaml:408` "`supervise.py:_band_verdict`". `src/basicly/working_set.py:285`. Replacement: "`working_set.py:_band_verdict`".
11. SUSPECTED. `decompose-plan/skill.yaml:65` "skills project to **three**" against `:84` "writes two roots"; `skills.py:47-50` has two default roots. Replacement: "the YAML source plus both projected roots - `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills`".

Verified correct, no change: `--runner` on run/advance/supervise, the 15-minute confirm TTL, rework n=2, `dep add` without `-t` refused, the label-write refusal, `needs-input.json`, the redirect file, the changelog categories, the four band verdicts, dot-to-hyphen worktree names.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN each finding is applied to the YAML source, THE PROJECTED SKILLS AND INSTRUCTIONS SHALL be rebuilt, and `uv run basicly check`, `uv run basicly skills-check --all-default-roots`, `uv run basicly agents-check`, `uv run basicly catalog lint` SHALL pass.
- WHEN the always-on fragment is corrected, THE PROJECTED `AGENTS.md` AND `.claude/CLAUDE.md` SHALL carry the eight-phase chain and no `teardown` or `retro` phase.
- WHEN finding 11 is checked, THE RECORD SHALL say which reading was right before the edit.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/skills/harness-loop/skill.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/skills/harness-client/skill.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/skills/catalog-authoring/skill.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/skills/decompose-plan/skill.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/skills/release-process/skill.yaml`
- `.basicly/core/fragments/project/harness-loop.fragment.yaml`
- `.claude/skills/**`
- `.agents/skills/**`
- `AGENTS.md`
- `.claude/CLAUDE.md`
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
- `.basicly/generated-manifest.json`

## Context

Read-only survey on 2026-08-26 of the nine loop skills (`.basicly/core/skills/*/skill.yaml`) and the four always-on fragments that mention the loop, the tracker, worktrees or gates, 61 claims checked against the code. Eleven are refuted; ten CONFIRMED by reading the code or `--help`, one SUSPECTED. Two would make an agent act wrongly (2, 4). Edit the YAML sources only, then `basicly skills-build --all-default-roots`, `basicly build`, and the projection gates.

1. `harness-client/skill.yaml:54-56` says `board serve` binds the loopback only and answers GET alone, a POST is 405. `src/basicly/board_cli.py:136` (`actions=not args.no_actions`, default on), `board_serve.py:402,411`, `board_actions.py:349` (405 only with `--no-actions`), `--bind` on `board serve --help`. Replacement: "It takes no lock and writes no file, but by default it registers one POST route that runs the basicly command an operator submits - pass `--no-actions` for an unattended wall, and leave `--bind` unset so it stays on the loopback."
2. `fragments/project/harness-loop.fragment.yaml` body: phases "(intake → classify → decompose → build → verify → ship → teardown → retro)". `src/basicly/loop_state.py:31` PHASES = intake, classify, decompose, build, verify, validate, ship, done; the `harness-loop` skill description itself says teardown and retro are not phases. Replacement: "(intake → classify → decompose → build → verify → validate → ship → done)".

4. `catalog-authoring/skill.yaml:41` "Project + verify: `basicly skills-build` then `basicly skills-check`." `src/basicly/skills.py:181-183` writes `.claude/skills` only without a flag; `basicly.toml:415-416` `projection-skills` checks both roots. Replacement: "A `VERDICT: not ready - ...` line joins every blocker it found with `; ` - a dirty base, an unrecognised config key, a metered runner with no token budget, a spent or unmeterable grant, an unapproved root checkpoint, or no open child in the band. Read the whole line."

9. `harness-loop/skill.yaml:194` ship row omits the demonstration guard. `loop.py:646-648` blocks ship with `needs_input="demonstration"` before the not-landed guard. Add: "Two guards run first and both block with no side effects: the recorded demonstration must still select something (`needs input: demonstration`), and the branch must already be merged."
10. `harness-loop/skill.yaml:408` "`supervise.py:_band_verdict`". `src/basicly/working_set.py:285`. Replacement: "`working_set.py:_band_verdict`".
11. SUSPECTED. `decompose-plan/skill.yaml:65` "skills project to **three**" against `:84` "writes two roots"; `skills.py:47-50` has two default roots. Replacement: "the YAML source plus both projected roots - `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills`".

payload.acceptance_criteria:
1. `policy checkpoint <name> --approve` records approval directly when stdin is an interactive TTY.
2. In a non-interactive context (no controlling TTY) with no confirm code, the command REFUSES to approve (non-zero exit, no marker recorded), and prints a one-time ephemeral confirm code plus the exact re-run command.
3. Re-running with `--confirm <code>` records the approval only when the code matches and has not expired (TTL); a wrong or expired code is refused with no marker recorded.
4. The gate covers all three checkpoints (classify, decompose, ship).
5. Confirm-code state is stored in the self-ignored .basicly/usage/ dir (never committed) using the same atomic write pattern as run-records.
6. TTY assumption verified: a tool-invoked Bash (Claude Code) has no controlling TTY on stdin/stdout/stderr; codex/copilot invoke Bash via the same piped-subprocess pattern (inferred, not directly exercised).
7. Deterministic and agent-agnostic; explicitly does NOT defeat a determined same-identity fork (the D1 shared-identity gap is out of scope) - it forces a deliberate second step that an autopilot directive will not contain.
payload.description:
From spike basicly-zv48 field incident (2026-07-17): a Claude Code fork inherited the full directive and autonomously drove the loop to ship+close (checkpoint --approve, loop advance) beyond its read-only mandate. Because the human session and its forks share one OS/git identity (the D1 gap), basicly cannot distinguish a rogue approval from an authorized one. Mitigation basicly can own: make policy checkpoint {classify,decompose,ship} --approve refuse in a non-interactive context (require a TTY or an ephemeral confirm-code the human types), so a subagent Bash without a controlling TTY cannot self-approve. Deterministic, agent-agnostic, aligns with the human-checkpoint intent. First task: verify the 'tool-invoked Bash has no TTY' assumption across claude/codex/copilot before relying on it as a floor. Complementary to attribution (basicly-z6dh run-record, basicly-140a). Does not prevent doc-writing/bead-filing (cheap, reversible) - only the consequential ship.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `policy checkpoint <name> --approve` records approval directly when stdin is an interactive TTY.
- In a non-interactive context (no controlling TTY) with no confirm code, the command refuses to approve (non-zero exit, no marker recorded) and prints a one-time ephemeral confirm code plus the exact re-run command.
- Re-running with `--confirm <code>` records the approval only when the code matches and has not expired; a wrong or expired code is refused with no marker recorded.
- The gate covers all three checkpoints (classify, decompose, ship).
- Confirm-code state lives in the self-ignored .basicly/usage/ dir using the same atomic write pattern as run-records.
- TTY assumption verified for Claude Code (no TTY on stdin/stdout/stderr); codex/copilot use the same piped-subprocess pattern (inferred).
- Deterministic and agent-agnostic; does not defeat a determined same-identity fork (D1 out of scope).
payload.design: Add a guarded-approval layer in policy.py. approve_checkpoint stays the raw recorder. New approve_checkpoint_guarded(repo_root, issue, name, *, interactive, confirm) returns an ApprovalResult(status in {approved,challenge,rejected}, code, detail). interactive True -> record + approved. Non-interactive + confirm None -> generate ephemeral code, store {issue:name -> {code, expires}} in .basicly/usage/checkpoint-confirms.json (atomic tmp-replace, self-ignored), return challenge with the code. Non-interactive + confirm -> consume-and-validate against stored code and TTL -> approved or rejected. Code generator and clock are module-level helpers (_new_code, _now) so tests monkeypatch them and the public signature stays under the 5-arg PLR0913 ceiling. CLI _cmd_policy_checkpoint detects sys.stdin.isatty(), passes interactive + --confirm, and maps ApprovalResult to output + exit code. TTL constant e.g. 900s.
payload.title: Governance: gate loop human-checkpoint approvals on interactive confirmation so a non-interactive/subagent process cannot self-approve ship
